name: Cowpea Bacterial Blight
description: A bacterial disease causing leaf spots, blighting, and stem lesions in cowpea. It is favored by warm, wet conditions and can cause significant defoliation and yield loss across West Africa.
symptoms: Water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown with yellow halos
Leaf lesions coalescing into large blighted areas
Stem and petiole lesions causing girdling
Premature defoliation starting from lower leaves
causes: Rain splash spreading bacteria between plants
Infected seeds serving as primary inoculum source
treatments: Apply copper-based bactericides (copper oxychloride) at first symptoms
Remove and destroy severely infected plants
Spray streptomycin where available and registered
prevention: Plant resistant cowpea varieties where available
Practice crop rotation with non-host crops
Remove and destroy crop debris after harvest
Avoid working in fields when plants are wet
